extracted.intended_audience: Commissioner of Indian Affairs, Interior Department officials, and United States Indian agents
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing an annual United States Indian Agency report describing the condition, progress, and needs of tribes (agriculture, education, health, law enforcement, improvements) and making policy/recommendation items for departmental action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of resident farmer
rubrics_metrics.description: "I would therefore suggest the propriety of the appointment of a man for this purpose, as a resident farmer for the Chippewas of Lake Superior, residing at L'Anse or vicinity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resident farmer should live among the Indians, work with them, direct and advise, assist in their work, care for and control teams — proposed to improve agricultural outcomes and teach cultivation to those unused to farming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use annuity funds for land improvements and make title inalienable
rubrics_metrics.description: "if the amount of money formerly paid in annuities... had been spent in honest improvements upon their lands, and the title to those lands had been made inalienable... there might have been thrift and competence."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spend former annuity payments on honest, permanent improvements to tribal lands and protect those lands from alienation to promote thrift and competence rather than frittering funds on transient goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide U.S. bonds for invested tribal funds and consult Indians on disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Chippewas of Lake Superior were much displeased at the refusal to give them United States bonds... As they only propose to have the interest used annually, this strikes me as a very reasonable request... they think they should be convened... and in formal council agree how many animals and tools and what kind they should receive."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider investing tribal funds in U.S. bonds with the interest distributed annually; consult the Indians in advance about disposition of invested funds and allow tribal input on how interest should be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage public school attendance and phase out government schools where public schools exist
rubrics_metrics.description: "as fast as there are schools organized in their neighborhoods the government schools should be discontinued and only such help be afforded as where the parents are too poor to provide them they be furnished the necessary books to pursue their studies."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shift education to district/public schools when available; provide materials (books/stationery) for children of poor parents to enable attendance; prioritize integration into local educational infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition distribution of government implements on demonstrated commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: "I made the qualification for receiving these articles depend on the recipient having built a house and put in a crop."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link receipt of government-provided wagons/cows and other implements to concrete acts demonstrating commitment to settled agriculture (e.g., building a house and planting a crop). Example: 32 recipients qualified and received items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold industrial expositions to stimulate and encourage industry
rubrics_metrics.description: "An exposition of the products and industry of the Indians of this reservation was held here... I think I may safely say that few local industrial fairs presented a greater variety... An annual repetition of a similar undertaking would greatly stimulate and encourage these Indians."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize local exhibitions of native agricultural, mechanical, and domestic products managed by Indians to foster pride, display skills, and stimulate industry; recommend annual repetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase mill capacity or build new mills rather than repair old ones
rubrics_metrics.description: "The capacity of the grist-mill will have to be increased to meet the growing wants... The mills in the Leech and Red Lake Reservations are old and unfit to meet the requirements... New mills should be built... as extensive repairs made upon the old ones would incur an expense nearly equal to that of new buildings."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess mill capacity and condition; favor construction of new mills when repairs approximate replacement cost to meet growing community needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage agricultural improvement via implements and incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: "Encouragement in the way of agricultural implements is one of the chief necessities to this end. Having fenced in a farm, if an Indian cannot procure necessary implements of labor, he becomes discouraged and relaxes to his old habits..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide agricultural implements and other material support once land is fenced or a farm is established to prevent discouragement and abandonment of farming in favor of nomadic pursuits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assure title or right of possession to improved land
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Indians are desirous that the title or right of possession to the land selected and improved by them should be in some way assured, and I deem it but just that it should so be done."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create legal assurance or recognized title/right of possession for Indians to lands they select and improve as a matter of justice and to encourage permanent settlement and investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use organized police force to maintain order and suppress liquor traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: "I cannot too highly commend the fidelity and efficiency of the police force... Their presence has contributed largely to the good order... The whisky traffic with the Indians under my charge has been nearly, if not quite, suppressed... All such offenders have been promptly dealt with."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and support a disciplined police force distributed across reservations to preserve order; actively detect and prosecute those introducing intoxicating liquors to reservations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach industrial arts alongside academic instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: "It would be of infinite advantage in promoting the civilization of the Indian to, in connection with what is now usually taught, also teach the rudiments of those industrial arts essential to the common conditions of life."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate practical industrial/artisan skills into school curricula to equip students with livelihoods and hasten self-supporting habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for policy that makes Indians self-supporting
rubrics_metrics.description: "...should the suggestions in my former reports be adopted by the department as its policy towards the Indians of this agency, but few years will elapse before they will become self-supporting..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt department policies and local measures focused on achieving self-sufficiency among Indians (through agriculture, education, property rights, and incentives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain accurate censuses and production/statistical estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: "The population is not made from a census, but estimated from the most reliable information I could procure... So also most of the productions are estimates... believed in all cases approximately correct, at any rate not overestimated."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile the best possible census and production statistics; note limitations and use conservative estimates to inform departmental decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep government structures and agency facilities in good repair
rubrics_metrics.description: "The structures belonging to the government are in good condition and repair and sufficient for the accommodation of employes."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure agency buildings, grist and saw mills, and other infrastructure are maintained or replaced as needed to support agency operations and Indian needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and facilitate missionary/religious instruction where beneficial
rubrics_metrics.description: "An increasing interest has been manifested by the Indians in religious matters, and the efforts of zealous men devoted to their spiritual salvation have been rewarded by many proselytes... I attribute much of the great improvement... to the beneficial effects of the teachings of these unselfish men..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide facilities or support for religious instruction when it demonstrably contributes to improved social and moral habits among the Indians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid forced removals that damage trust and productive efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Account of forced military removal of a hunting camp: removal caused great loss of meat and death of horses and created bitterness; agent states that aiding removal would have damaged his influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid involuntary or forced removals of Indians (e.g., hunting camps) on flimsy complaints, as such actions can destroy years of progress and trust; agents should resist or not aid unjust removals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require return of property captured in raids when claimed to preserve peace
rubrics_metrics.description: "I made it known that all horses thus obtained must be returned when claimed, and this has been done."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and enforce clear rules that property taken in raids must be returned upon claim to reduce cycles of retaliation and maintain order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply proceeds of land sales/treaties to assist in housing and farm development
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding proposed Crow treaty sale: "Then let a portion of the fund be applied in assisting a few more Indians to build houses and open farms, and a long step will have been taken in the solution of this difficult problem of Crow civilization."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When land is sold by treaty, allocate a portion of proceeds to tangible investments (houses, farms, implements) that help tribes transition to settled agriculture and self-support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use distribution of domestic animals and wagons as inducement to settle
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of wagons and cows to Indians who qualified by building a house and putting in a crop: "On the 5th July I had the satisfaction of distributing to thirty-two Indians thus qualified."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute livestock and transportation implements selectively as incentives tied to concrete settlement and farming actions to encourage permanent improvements.
